Custom Colour (Hex) contributes hue and saturation only. Its value component is ignored on purpose so that Brightness (%) owns level and a colour can be dimmed without shifting hue.
Reported Colour is a passive readout of what a bound light last reported. The driver never re-applies from a report, so it does not detect or correct a light that has drifted.

The guarantee this driver actually makes is the published name: COLOUR_NAME is always correct, so no decision has to rest on the colour being seen.

Next Hue and Previous Hue clear Custom Colour (Hex). The hex outranks the hue stop, so a step underneath one would move the selection and change nothing in the room; a step is treated as an explicit request for a named stop.
Brighter and Dimmer only reach a fixture when Set Light Level is Yes. With it set to No the level is recorded and published but never sent, and Status says so.
Presets live in PersistData, which is not exported with a Composer project. Restoring a project onto a different controller starts with four empty slots.

The driver does not stream or bundle audio. It routes the room to your chosen source, sets the cue level, and publishes the cue's media reference; your Composer programming (or an always-on source) starts the actual file.
A room reports no end-of-media callback, so cue length is the fixed Cue Hold Seconds timer rather than the true file duration. Set it slightly longer than your longest cue.

The room commands used (SELECT_AUDIO_DEVICE, SET_VOLUME_LEVEL, ROOM_OFF) and the CURRENT_VOLUME / CURRENT_SELECTION room variables are the Control4 room-proxy surface; they have not yet been confirmed on a physical controller for this driver.

If a room's CURRENT_VOLUME cannot be read the cue still plays, but that zone is neither volume- nor power-restored - an unreadable room is treated as unknown, never as 'was off' - and a Zone Unavailable event fires.

Restore-after-restart replays the persisted levels once at driver init. A room changed by hand between the restart and that replay is overwritten.

features: Official UniFi Network Integration API only (/proxy/network/integration/v1) — no reverse-engineered legacy endpoints
Stateless X-API-KEY auth with a key the customer mints on their own console — no cloud dependency, no vendor-issued credential
Controller reachability + application version, with Controller Went Online / Offline events
Site device health: total / online / offline adopted-device counts, with UniFi Device Went Offline and All UniFi Devices Online events
Named-client presence: up to three watched client MACs, each with Came Online / Went Offline events and a BOOL variable, debounced against brief Wi-Fi drops
One guarded control action: power-cycle a PoE switch port to reboot a stuck camera, AP, or doorbell — off by default, license-gated
LAN-only destination safeguard, the API key is never written to the log, and MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing

compatibility.label: Control4 OS
compatibility.value: 3.0.0 or newer (HTTPS to a self-signed console needs the C4:url TLS options — OS 3.2.0+; see limitations)

compatibility.label: UniFi console
compatibility.value: UniFi OS console (UDM / UDR / UCG / UX / UniFi OS Server) running a current Network application — API keys do not exist on the legacy self-hosted Java controller

compatibility.label: API
compatibility.value: UniFi Network Integration API v1, local HTTPS on port 443 (11443 on UniFi OS Server)

compatibility.label: State feedback
compatibility.value: Polled (default 30s); no push channel is documented in the Integration API

requirements: A UniFi OS console on the same LAN as the controller, with the Network application running
An API key generated by the customer in the Network app (Settings → Control Plane → Integrations) — it inherits the creating admin's permissions
The Site ID (use the List Sites action to enumerate them)
For the PoE power-cycle action: the switch's device id (List Devices action) and the port number, plus Enable PoE Power Cycle = Yes
For production, an IntegrateIT license key bound to this controller
limitations: Release Candidate: verified against the Control4 API simulator; acceptance on a physical UniFi console and Control4 controller is not yet attached to this release.

TLS reality: UniFi consoles present a self-signed certificate. By default the driver sets the C4:url ssl_verify_peer/ssl_verify_host options to off, which is what makes a self-signed console reachable — the simulator does not model TLS, so this specific behavior is verified on hardware, not in the sim. Fingerprint pinning is not offered because the Control4 URL API has no documented pin option; the alternative is TLS Verification = Full with a console certificate the controller OS trusts.

On OS builds without C4:url() the driver falls back to the legacy urlGet/urlPost path, which has no per-request TLS options — a self-signed console will likely be unreachable there. Practical floor for self-signed consoles is an OS with C4:url().

Presence and device-health scanning read up to 200 entries per poll (one page). On a site whose client or device list exceeds one page, the driver holds state rather than inventing it: a watched client absent from the page it fetched is kept at its last-known presence (never false-declared offline), and device-health change events are suppressed until a full page is seen again. The trade-off on such large sites is that a watched client which genuinely leaves may not raise Went Offline until it once again fits within a single page.

Presence is polled, not pushed: a watched phone joining or leaving is seen on the next poll (default 30s), then offline is debounced by the Offline After (polls) setting to ride out brief Wi-Fi drops.

The PoE power-cycle action requires the target port to actually deliver PoE; the console accepts the action per its own firmware rules and the driver surfaces the HTTP result. It is the only write this driver performs, and it is disabled until Enable PoE Power Cycle is set to Yes.
API keys exist only on UniFi OS consoles — the legacy self-hosted Java controller is not supported, by Ubiquiti's design.

compatibility.value: UniFi OS console running UniFi Protect with the Integration API (UNVR, UDM-Pro/SE, UCG, Cloud Key G2+)

compatibility.value: Protect releases publishing the Integration API v1 (spec v7.1.x); probed via GET /v1/meta/info

compatibility.label: Event feed
compatibility.value: Polled over HTTPS (default 3s); realtime WebSocket push is not implemented in v0.1.0

requirements: A UniFi OS console running UniFi Protect, reachable on the same LAN as the controller
The console's IP address (reserve it in DHCP) and an API key created in UniFi OS → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations
At least one adopted Protect camera; a G4/G5 Doorbell for ring events
For production, an IntegrateIT license key bound to this controller
limitations: Release Candidate: verified against the Control4 API simulator; acceptance on a physical UniFi console and cameras is not yet attached to this release.

Events only — this driver surfaces Protect activity to Control4 programming. It does not show video, provision RTSPS streams, take snapshots, or control cameras/PTZ. Navigator camera viewing is out of scope.

Event feed is POLLED, not pushed: Protect publishes motion/smart/ring events on a WebSocket subscription (GET /v1/subscribe/events); this version polls that endpoint over plain HTTPS on the configured interval instead of holding a WebSocket. Event latency is up to one poll interval, and consoles that answer the event path only after a WebSocket upgrade will reject the poll — the driver then reports it in Event Feed status, and camera-online/offline events (from GET /v1/cameras) keep working. Realtime WebSocket push is planned, not in v0.1.0.
Camera-offline detection derives from the console's reported per-camera connection state on the camera poll (default 30s), so it trails reality by up to one camera-poll interval.

The console's HTTPS certificate is self-signed; the driver skips TLS certificate verification by default (set Verify TLS Certificate = Yes only for consoles with a valid certificate). On very old OS builds without the modern URL API the legacy HTTP fallback cannot relax TLS verification and may fail against self-signed consoles.
The Site Manager cloud proxy path (api.ui.com) is not used — this driver is local-console only. Non-LAN console addresses are refused unless Allow WAN Console is explicitly set to Yes.
